title: I updated my AI video to sprite sheet tool - MP4 to Sprite
author: Super-Wolverine447
selftext:
*I’ve been working on a workflow for turning AI-generated videos into sprite sheets, and I ran into a common problem: low-resolution output often loses important details around edges, shadows, and glowing effects.*

*To improve that, I tested:*

*- a pixel mode with harder edges*

*- better background edge cleanup*

*- smarter color control for 32x32 / 64x64 output*

*I’m curious how others handle this problem.*  

*What do you usually do to keep sprite sheets clean at low resolution without losing too much detail?*  
*I posted the demo and full details on my itchio page for anyone interested.*

replies.author: Super-Wolverine447
replies.body: My tool actually can process videos with different resolutions. The free demo version (V2.4) does support semi-transparency. However, I feel like the semi-transparent results look really blurry, especially when outputting at low resolutions like 32x32 or 64x64. So, I tried making the low-res output use opaque, pixelated processing instead, and it ends up looking much more like characters you’d see in a pixel game.

comments.author: HyoTwelve
comments.body:
I've had the same problem and tried to solve it with multiple strategies. But nothing gives perfect results, for example I tried: 
- applying rembg to every frames is simlpe but background artifacts might stay.
- chroma based removal works great but the color of the sprite changes, even if you use the mask you get then you still don't handle blended pixels.
- "flood-fill" approaches are decent too but it doesn't handle holes inside the model easily and needs threshold value tweaks? Also impossible to handle ambiguous pixels...
Basically what we need is something that does more than "cut-out" frames, but it should actually fix the edges too and "repaint" the sprite details cleanly where required... Could your tool be doing that? Image editing-models such as gemini are able to do this somewhat well but it's quite expensive running across tons of frames and a bit inconsistent. I don't have the ressources to fine-tune a model for this but wondering is someone would tackle this seriously...


Also, a thing that helped a bit for me was simply generating higher resolution videos to have less "blended pixels" where the background is unclear, but the cost increases...

comments.body: I still don’t know how to do this :( what video generator do you use ?

replies.author: Super-Wolverine447
replies.body:
You can use any AI to generate a short video of a few seconds. Just design the first frame yourself and let the AI generate actions like walking or jumping.

The crucial part is using a solid single-color background. It’s best to use a color that completely contrasts with your character’s edges (usually, white works fine). Also, to make sure the actions don’t go out of frame, keep your character’s height at around 70% of the canvas. Make sure to tell the AI not to move the character and to keep them centered.

These are the basic guidelines, feel free to give it a go!
